title: Kummer etale morphisms are stable under fs base change
statement: Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a Kummer etale morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes: log etale in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and with injective characteristic maps whose target elements have positive multiples in the image, as in [def-per-kummer-log-morphism]. Let $g:(Y',M_{Y'})\to(Y,M_Y)$ be any morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes assume that the ordinary scheme fibre product $X\times_YY'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is locally Noetherian, and form the fs log fibre product $(X',M_{X'})=(X,M_X)\times_Y^{\rm fs}(Y',M_{Y'})$, a locally Noetherian fs log scheme finite over $X\times_YY'$. Then the projection $f':(X',M_{X'})\to(Y',M_{Y'})$ is again Kummer etale. No flatness, strictness, or triviality of the log structure on $Y'$ is required.

source.place: Expose X, proof of 1.8 and the parenthetical assertion after diagram (1.a), printed pp.146--147: Kummer etale G-covers are stable under any fs base change; fs-cartesian diagram from Expose VIII 5.3.8, p.125.

proof.text: By [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison], the fs product exists and is locally Noetherian with finite comparison to the assumed locally Noetherian ordinary product. Choose affine chart neighbourhoods $U\to V$ for $f$ using [lem-per-kummer-etale-local-chart-criterion], with $h:P\to Q$, finite cokernel $C$ killed by $n$ invertible on $V$, and etale $c:U\to B=V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$. Strict etale chart neighbourhoods pull back to ordinary etale neighbourhoods: the strict clause of [lem-per-fs-product-finite-comparison] identifies these fs products with ordinary products, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] gives the covering property. It therefore suffices to give such chart data after base change on each of these neighbourhoods.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72, local standard-cover description; X 1.8, pp.146--147, local base-change assertion.

proof.text: Replace $Y'$ locally by an affine etale neighbourhood $V'$ mapping to $V$. The chart-refinement clause of [lem-per-kummer-saturated-pushout-algebra] supplies an fs chart $R$ on $V'$ and a compatible $a:P\to R$. Put $S_0=Q\oplus_PR$ and $S=(S_0^{\rm int})^{\rm sat}$. The same node states that $R\to S$ and its group map are injective, every element of $S$ has a positive multiple in $R$, and $S^{\rm gp}/R^{\rm gp}\simeq C$. Thus this cokernel is finite, killed by the same $n$, which remains invertible on $V'$ because a ring homomorphism takes an inverse of $n$ to an inverse of its image.

Write $F=U\times_VV'$ and $D=V'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S]$. The fs-product chart formula of [lem-per-kummer-saturated-pushout-algebra] identifies the local pullback with
$$U'=F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S_0]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S],$$
with chart $S$. There is a canonical ordinary-scheme identification $U'=U\times_BD$. Indeed, writing $H=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$, $A=\Gamma(V',\mathcal O)$ and $T=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$, the two coordinate rings are
$$(T\otimes_H A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z[S_0]}\mathbf Z[S],\qquad T\otimes_{H\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S]).$$
A map from either ring to a ring $E$ is a triple of maps $T,A,\mathbf Z[S]\to E$: the first two agree on $H$, and their monomial values agree with the third on $Q,R$, respectively. Agreement on $P$ is included in agreement on $H$; the pushout relations of $S_0$ impose exactly these equations. This proves the identification compatibly with all projections.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, p.107, chart base change; X 1.8 diagram (1.a).

proof.text: Consequently $c':U'\to D$ is the ordinary base change of $c:U\to B$. All these schemes are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] proves that $c'$ is etale. The compatible charts $R\to S$ have the injectivity, root-cofinality and invertible finite cokernel from Step 2. They therefore satisfy the converse of [lem-per-kummer-etale-local-chart-criterion]. The strict etale neighbourhoods used above cover $X'$, so that criterion applied to this family proves globally that $f'$ is Kummer etale. The integer $n$ was pulled back only as a unit; no flatness or strictness of $g$ was used.

source.place: VI 2.2, p.72; X 1.8, p.147. Ordinary etale ring base change: Stacks Tag 00U2 (algebra.tex, lemma-etale, item (2)).
